Change c0300. Location: 1818 Vol. II, Ch. VIII; 1831 Ch. XVI.

Context before (unchanged): It was apparent that my conversation had interested the father in my behalf, and I was a fool in having exposed my person to the horror of his children.

1818 text: I ought to have familiarized the old De Lacy to me, and by degrees have discovered myself to the rest of his family, when they should have been prepared for my approach.

1831 text: I ought to have familiarised the old De Lacey to me, and by degrees to have discovered myself to the rest of his family, when they should have been prepared for my approach.

Diff: I ought to have [-familiarized-] {+familiarised+} the old De [-Lacy-] {+Lacey+} to me, and by degrees {+to+} have discovered myself to the rest of his family, when they should have been prepared for my approach.

Context after (unchanged): But I did not believe my errors to be irretrievable; and, after much consideration, I resolved to return to the cottage, seek the old man, and by my representations win him to my party.

result.rationale: Mostly orthography: 'familiarized' becomes 'familiarised' and 'De Lacy' becomes 'De Lacey'. The only wording change is the added infinitive marker 'to' in 'to discover', which is a grammatical smoothing with no change of meaning.
